message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code (Title 2, Subtitle B). Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights | Notes | |----------|-----------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords must itemize deductions and provide receipts if requested. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition; repair plumbing, heating, electrical, structural issues, etc. | If landlord fails to fix major problems, tenants may withhold rent or pursue repairs themselves and recover costs. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice (usually 24‑hour written notice) except in emergencies. | Notice must specify time and purpose. | | **Anti‑Discrimination** | • Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or handicap. | Also applies to advertising, leasing, and terms. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for residential leases >1 year.
• Lease must include rent amount, due date, security deposit, and other material terms. | Oral agreements can be enforceable but harder to prove. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but must give proper notice (typically 30 days for month‑to‑month, 90 days for longer leases). | Some cities have local rent‑control ordinances. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow court procedure: serve notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment), file unlawful detainer action, obtain judgment, then sheriff executes eviction. | Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Repair and Deduct / Withhold Rent** | • If landlord fails to repair, tenant may pay for repairs and deduct cost from rent, or withhold rent until repairs done. | Must keep receipts and notify landlord in writing. | | **Disclosure Requirements** | • Landlord must disclose lead‑based paint hazards if property built before 1978. | Must provide pamphlet and disclosure form. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Tenants may sublet or assign lease only with landlord’s consent unless lease says otherwise. | Consent can’t be unreasonably withheld. | | **Move‑in/Move‑out Inspection** | • Landlord must provide move‑in inspection report; tenant can note existing damage. | Helps avoid disputes over security deposit. | ### Practical Steps If You Encounter Problems 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of lease, notices, emails, photos of conditions, repair requests, and receipts. 2. **Written Requests** – Send repair requests in writing (email or certified mail) so there’s proof of communication. 3. **Know Your Notice Periods** – For example, a 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for ending a month‑to‑month tenancy. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you’re facing eviction or a dispute, contact a local tenant‑rights organization or legal aid office. Many offer free consultations. ### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Provides consumer guides and complaint filing forms. - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – Offers resources on fair housing and landlord‑tenant law. - **Local County Clerk’s Office** – For filing or responding to unlawful detainer actions. - **Legal Aid Societies** – e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, Houston Legal Aid Society, etc. --- If you need a formal document—such as a lease agreement, a notice of intent to terminate, or a repair request letter—I can help draft it. Just let me know which type of document you’d like and any specific details you want included.
